finding.title: Add points_ledger and reward_redemptions to write_payloads.json and the PHASE D zero-denial oracle in firestore_rules.test.mjs

evidence.quote: "_comment": "Canonical per-collection write-payload fixtures derived from Dart codec encode() outputs...",

finding.why: write_payloads.json's own header calls PAYLOADS 'the single source of truth for valid doc shapes, consumed by Phase D and E,' and PHASE D's comment claims 'a legitimate owner must be able to write every whitelisted collection without a single permission-denied error... the zero-denial oracle catches it before it reaches production.' In reality the fixture enumerates 12 collections and PHASE D enumerates 15 (ending at curriculum_scopes, line 767-768) — points_ledger and reward_redemptions are absent from both, and (verified in tool/emit_fixture_payloads.dart, not in this batch) the generator's payloads map has no entry for either, confirming the omission is systematic. Neither collection has a hasOnly whitelist today so nothing is silently broken right now, but this exact rules file has independently hit the 'hasOnly whitelist drops a real field → permission-denied in production' bug three times for other collections (profile_programs.updated_at, curriculum_tracks.purged/purged_at, bookmarks.track_type — all documented in this file's own comments). Since points_ledger/reward_redemptions are the most obvious remaining candidates for a future hasOnly addition (every sibling snapshot/ledger collection already has one), the safety net built specifically to catch that failure mode has a blind spot exactly where the next occurrence is most likely.
finding.recommendation: Add points_ledger and reward_redemptions payloads to tool/emit_fixture_payloads.dart's map, regenerate write_payloads.json via `make emit-fixtures`, and add both to PHASE D's oracle list and PHASE E's round-trip table.
acceptance_criteria: write_payloads.json gains `points_ledger` and `reward_redemptions` keys after `make emit-fixtures`
PHASE D's owner-write-succeeds test includes both new PAYLOADS entries

finding.title: Delete the dead test/firestore-rules/ Jest suite, superseded by functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs
finding.why: This suite is fully dead: ci.yml (lines 303-307, confirmed) only ever runs functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs, and this directory is invoked by no Makefile target. If anyone ran `npm test` here today every '[allow]' case would fail — it targets top-level `accounts`/`learner_profiles`/`track_configs`/`completion_events` collections that do not exist anywhere in the live nested users/{uid}/learner_profiles/{profileId}/... rules (confirmed by a full read of firestore.rules); they would all hit the global default-deny. Meanwhile docs/architecture.md:575, docs/development-guide.md:87, docs/deployment-guide.md:51 and docs/test-options.md:38 still describe `test/firestore-rules/` (Jest) as the live firestore-rules CI job, and docs/api-contracts.md:84 claims deprecated top-level rule blocks are 'retained because... test/firestore-rules/ pin them' — those blocks don't exist in firestore.rules at all. A contributor trusting any of those docs and editing this directory expecting it to gate CI wastes their change; the directory also drags in a fully duplicate devDependency set (jest, firebase, @firebase/rules-unit-testing) plus a committed package-lock.json for zero live test value.
finding.recommendation: Delete test/firestore-rules/ (all 4 git-tracked files including package-lock.json) now that functions/test/firestore_rules.test.mjs is the confirmed canonical suite — the file's own header comment already says this is the intended endpoint ('kept only for reference until removed').
acceptance_criteria: test/firestore-rules/ directory removed from the tree (git rm)
The 4 canonical docs referencing test/firestore-rules/ as the live CI path are updated in the same change or a follow-up doc-drift ticket is filed

finding.title: Assert update (not just delete) fails in the diagnostic_logs append-only test in firestore_rules.test.mjs
finding.rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what source can do wrong)

evidence.quote: test('update and delete are denied even for owner (append-only)', async () => {

finding.why: The test's name and its own inline comment both assert the author's intent to verify update-denial, but the body only calls `deleteDoc` — no `setDoc`/update attempt against the pre-seeded doc is ever made. If a future rules edit accidentally changes diagnostic_logs's `allow update: if false;` to `if isOwner(uid);` (matching most sibling collections in the same rules file, which DO allow owner update), this test stays green. diagnostic_logs holds diagnostic event data for a children's-app account; losing its append-only guarantee unnoticed is exactly the class of regression this suite exists to catch, and here it doesn't.
finding.recommendation: Add `await assertFails(setDoc(doc(owner(), `users/${OWNER}/diagnostic_logs/e1`), { msg: 'changed' }));` against the pre-seeded doc inside this test.
acceptance_criteria: The diagnostic_logs 'update and delete are denied' test asserts both an update attempt and a delete attempt fail
Test goes red if diagnostic_logs's `allow update: if false;` in firestore.rules is changed to `if isOwner(uid);`

finding.title: De-duplicate hand-typed matrix literals from write_payloads.json PAYLOADS in firestore_rules.test.mjs (stage_definitions.track_id, study_day_configs.day_type)
finding.why: The file's own comment at line 459-461 documents a real incident: 'A stale fixture carrying track_type made this rules test red on dev... invisible because test-rules isn't wired into make ci.' That incident is exactly this pattern repeating: the hand-typed Path-13 `validStage` literal encodes `track_id` as a STRING ('t1') while the codec-derived PAYLOADS.stage_definitions fixture (the file's own stated 'single source of truth') encodes it as a NUMBER (1); similarly Path-22's `validConfig.day_type` is 'learning' while PAYLOADS.study_day_configs.day_type (used by PHASE E, line 844) is 'study'. Neither copy is cross-checked against the other. Today neither divergence trips a rule (hasOnly only checks key names, not value types), so nothing is currently broken — this is a latent maintenance trap that reproduces the file's own documented failure mode, not a live bug.
finding.recommendation: Derive the Path-13/Path-22 matrix literals from PAYLOADS (spread + override, as PHASE D/E already do) instead of hand-typing a second copy, or add an explicit comment cross-referencing the fixture so a schema change prompts updating both.
acceptance_criteria: stage_definitions and study_day_configs matrix-test literals are sourced from PAYLOADS or explicitly comment-linked to it so one edit updates both

finding.title: Fix no_feature_cross_import's _isBarrel to match the documented providers.dart crossing point (or fix the doc)

evidence.quote: The single allowed crossing point is `features/<feature>/providers.dart`, which is the deliberate, documented public surface.

static bool _isBarrel(String importedFeature, String importedPath) {
    return importedPath == '$importedFeature.dart';

test('does not recognise providers.dart as barrel', () {
        expect(_isBarrel('tracks', 'providers.dart'), isFalse);

finding.why: docs/coding-standards.md Rule 2 and this package's own README both tell developers/agents the only sanctioned cross-feature import is `features/<feature>/providers.dart`. No such file exists anywhere in the repo (grep confirms zero `providers.dart` under lib/features/); the real, consistently-used barrel across all 15 features is `features/<feature>/<feature>.dart`, which is what `_isBarrel` actually checks and what the parallel root-Makefile audit check 15 also accepts. A contributor who follows the written standard to fix a warn-only Rule-2 violation would create `providers.dart`, and the lint (once unbricked) would still reject it — the test file even asserts this outcome explicitly (`_isBarrel('tracks', 'providers.dart')` is `isFalse`).
finding.recommendation: Pick one source of truth and make all three artifacts agree: either rename the real convention to `providers.dart` project-wide, or update docs/coding-standards.md Rule 2 and packages/custom_lints/README.md to document `<feature>.dart` as the actual barrel. Cheapest fix: update the two docs (README.md Rule 2 section + coding-standards.md Rule 2, the latter outside this batch) to say `<feature>.dart`.
acceptance_criteria: packages/custom_lints/README.md Rule 2 section and docs/coding-standards.md Rule 2 name the same barrel filename that no_feature_cross_import.dart's _isBarrel actually accepts.
no_feature_cross_import_test.dart's barrel-name assertions match the corrected documented convention.
dart test in packages/custom_lints still passes.
